evidence.quote: Polycab has transitioned from a market-leading wires & cables manufacturer into a diversified electrical goods powerhouse.
FY26 revenue crossed ₹28,884 Cr (29% YoY), EBITDA grew 35% YoY, and PAT grew 32% YoY — all at the highest-ever levels.
The company is executing 'Project Spring' (FY30 roadmap) targeting 1.5x industry growth, ₹60-80 Bn cumulative capex, FMEG margins of 8-10%, and exports >10% of revenue.
Core product/service: Wires and Cables (W&C), Fast-Moving Electrical Goods (FMEG), and EPC services.
Polycab is both a core product provider (W&C) and an EPC contractor, enabling it to capture value at multiple points in the infrastructure value chain.
Polycab's EPC segment order book (₹10,900 Cr combined BharatNet + RDSS) and the fact that EPC revenues grew 143% YoY in FY25 directly attributable to RDSS execution shows on-ground momentum.

Polycab is deploying aggressive capex while maintaining a fortress balance sheet — a classic setup for sustained earnings compounding followed by PE expansion once the market fully prices in the FMEG + EPC + export growth stories.
Polycab's backward integration (100% in W&C, 90% in FMEG), 30-31% market share, and 94-country export presence make it the only Indian company positioned to capture all these trends simultaneously.
Polycab's revenue grew 29% in FY26. Q1 FY27 grew 39%. Both are well above the 20-25% threshold.

Polycab operates structurally above the norm (13-14%) due to: Massive scale (2× the next largest competitor — KEI), Near-total backward integration, 3,900+ distributor network providing pricing power.
